{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{distinguish|Harry Levine}}
'''Harold I. Levine''' was an American [[mathematician]] who was professor at [[Stanford University]]. He specialized in [[wave motion]] and [[optics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://math.stanford.edu/directory/faculty.html |title=Department of Mathematics - Stanford University |website=math.stanford.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061205091734/http://math.stanford.edu/directory/faculty.html |archive-date=2006-12-05}} </ref>

Levine was born in [[New York City]]. After he graduated from the [[City College of New York]], he earned a [[Ph.D.]] in Physics from [[Cornell University]]. In 1954, he was awarded a [[Guggenheim fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=l&page=9 |title=All Fellows - John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |access-date=2010-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622023505/http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=l&page=9 |archive-date=2011-06-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Levine died on December 10, 2017, at the age of 95.<ref>[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/sfgate/obituary.aspx?pid=187529723 Harold Levine]</ref><ref>[https://www.bookfinder.com/author/harold-levine/ Harold Levine Books]</ref>
